pronunciation.title: Say it right from day one

rules.explain: a=AH, e=EH, i=EE, o=OH, u=OO. Always. So CASA is KAH-sah.

examples.t: casa
examples.r: KAH-sah
examples.en: house

examples.t: mesa
examples.r: MEH-sah
examples.en: table

rules.rule: H is silent, J sounds like H
rules.explain: HOLA is OH-lah (no H sound). J in JUEVES sounds like English H: HWEH-vehs.

examples.t: hola
examples.r: OH-lah
examples.en: hello

examples.t: jueves
examples.r: HWEH-vehs
examples.en: Thursday

rules.explain: Ñ is like NY in canyon: NIÑO = NEEN-yoh. LL and Y sound like Y in yes.

examples.t: niño
examples.r: NEEN-yoh
examples.en: boy

examples.t: calle
examples.r: KAH-yeh
examples.en: street

rules.explain: Tap your tongue once for R. PERRO (dog) rolls longer than PERO (but).

examples.t: pero
examples.r: PEH-roh
examples.en: but

examples.t: perro
examples.r: PEH-rroh
examples.en: dog

rules.explain: Most words stress the middle: HOLA = OH-lah, GRACIAS = GRAH-syahs. An accent mark (á) forces stress there.

examples.t: gracias
examples.r: GRAH-syahs
examples.en: thanks

examples.t: café
examples.r: kah-FEH
examples.en: coffee

alphabet.title: The Polish alphabet: 24 letters, eight with diacritics
alphabet.explain: Polish uses the Latin alphabet plus eight letters with marks: ą ć ę ł ń ó ś ź ż. The marks change the sound — ś is s, ź is z with a soft tongue, and ł is the w of wine.

letters.tip: ts with a soft tongue: ćma
s with a soft tongue: śnieg

counting.title: Counting in Polish: 0 to 15
counting.explain: Learn 0-12 by heart. Thirteen and up is the number + -naście: trzynaście, czternaście, piętnaście.
rules: Consonant clusters are normal: wstrzymać (to stop) starts with five consonants in a row.
ł is English w; ź ż ś c are soft variants of z s and ts.
Stress falls on the second-to-last syllable: dwa-NA-scie, trze-NA-scie.
